entities.summary: The Battle of Oak Grove, also known as the Battle of French's Field or King's School House, took place on June 25, 1862, in Henrico County, Virginia, the first of the Seven Days Battles of the American Civil War. Maj. Gen. George B. McClellan advanced his lines with the objective of bringing Richmond within range of his siege guns. Two Union divisions of the III Corps attacked across the headwaters of White Oak Swamp, but were repulsed by Maj. Benjamin Huger's Confederate division. McClellan, who was 3 miles (4.8 km) in the rear, initially telegraphed to call off the attack, but ordered another attack over the same ground when he arrived at the front.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Battle of Oak Grove was a pivotal engagement in the Seven Days Battles of the American Civil War, resulting in significant Confederate victories and forcing Maj. Gen. George B. McClellan to withdraw his forces from Richmond.
